acceptanceCriteria.text: An authorized orchestrator can launch a named Backlog card through either CLI or MCP, then claim it with the existing claim_kanban_card command without a desktop Play action.

A caller can explicitly launch multiple card IDs in one request; invalid or ineligible inputs produce actionable per-card errors and no partial mutation, while duplicate IDs and retried requests cannot create duplicate launches or attempts.

Reader, planner and worker callers and revoked/expired grants cannot launch cards; existing active claims, Ready for review and Done cards are not reset or overwritten, and human-only review powers remain unchanged.

CLI discovery and MCP tool discovery expose the new command and its authorization/input contract; CLI runbook and role guidance describe external single/batch launch and distinguish launch from claim and approval.
Behavioral regressions and the required delivery gate pass; disposable-project CLI and MCP smoke evidence demonstrates launch followed by claim/submission and unauthorized rejection.

body:
## Goal
An orchestrator explicitly asked to burn down Kanban cards must be able to launch them from an external chat through the supported CLI/MCP API, without requiring desktop Play for each card. Today all incomplete cards can be Backlog with playPending=false, leaving claim_kanban_card blocked. This is a requested product authorization-policy change, not permission to bypass current guards during implementation.

## Scope
Add a shared launch command exposed through both CLI discovery/calls and MCP. Let an authorized orchestrator launch one card or an explicit nonempty list of card IDs, then use the existing claim/heartbeat/submit workflow. Use the normal queued/claimable Play transition without spawning duplicate desktop chats for an external caller. Validate and authorize the entire batch before mutation; reject invalid or ineligible IDs with actionable per-card errors and no partial launch. Make retries idempotent and preserve active claims and completed/submitted work. Require explicit card IDs; no implicit launch-all. Keep reader/planner/worker access denied, token/grant checks intact, and approval, kick-back, deletion and checkpoint powers human-only. Update capability discovery, command/tool descriptions, CLI runbook and role guidance to reflect this deliberate policy change. Do not implement the cards being launched or change epic execution.

## Tests
Write failing behavioral tests first for authorized single/batch launch followed by successful existing claim; rejected unauthorized callers; mixed-invalid batch atomicity; duplicate IDs and repeated requests; active/Ready for review/Done card protection; and revoked/expired grants. Cover CLI and MCP command exposure using existing integration conventions.

## Verification
Run the delivery-standards full gate, including Fireguard when tests change. Smoke the supported CLI and MCP against a disposable initialized project: launch explicitly named cards, claim and submit one, observe Ready for review, and prove unauthorized launch is refused. Do not launch real Backlog cards as test fixtures.
expectedArtifacts: Shared authorized Kanban launch command and capability policy
CLI and MCP exposure with behavioral regression coverage
Updated CLI runbook and role guidance
title: Allow authorized orchestrators to launch Kanban cards through CLI and MCP
